title: The biggest risk in carbon credits is counting the same tonne twice
format: Landscape 1920x1080, 30 fps, about 90 seconds. YouTube, LinkedIn, X, website hero
voice_draft: macOS say, Daniel (en_GB). Final: Rume's own voice cloned in ElevenLabs from media/brand/voice-samples, see README

caption: COUNTED
TWICE
scenes.line: Everyone is selling carbon credits. But the biggest risk isn't the price. It is the same tonne, counted twice.

caption: 26 SETS
OF BOOKS
scenes.line: There are about twenty six carbon registries. Each one keeps its own books, so one tonne can turn up in two of them, and nobody sees it.

caption: ONE
REGISTER
scenes.line: I'm Rume Dominic, and that is why we built CarbonLedger. One register on Solana, where every gram gets a serial number, and can be retired only once.

caption: IN THE
CODE
scenes.line: The rules are not a promise on a slide. They live in the code. The same ten test cases run on the server, the database, and the program on chain.

caption: CHECK IT
YOURSELF
scenes.line: Every retirement gets a receipt, sealed to the one before it. One fingerprint goes on Solana, so anyone can check it, without trusting us.

caption: EVERY
GRAM
scenes.line: In the app, you scan your shopping, or add a journey, and see your estimated footprint, in grams. No crypto wallet needed.

caption: THE SMALLEST
FIRST
scenes.line: Then it becomes a game. Every gram is a point. Together, we can clear the smallest country's pilot target first, and right now that is Kiribati. Or you can retire for any country you choose.

caption: PILOT
UNITS
scenes.line: To be clear, today these are pilot units, not yet verified credits. The record is real. What comes next: we link each batch to its evidence, field video and satellite imagery, and a named verifier signs it off.

caption: AT A
TIME
scenes.line: Imagine a ledger where the world pays down its carbon debt, one gram at a time. Click the link below, and join the movement.
